newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks boosted by bullish Goldman strategist.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks boosted by bullish Goldman strategist.

text.p: U.S. stocks rallied late Tuesday after word filtered through Wall Street that Goldman Sachs strategist Abby Joseph Cohen remained positive on the outlook for U.S. stocks, comparing the market's recent pullback to a flu shot.
The S&P rose 3.99 Tuesday to 766.12 while the Dow industrials rose 53 points to 6609.
"This has been a very dramatic period...but we remain optimistic about the U.S. market outlook," Cohen said on a call to clients, later made available on a recording.

Cohen, who has become one of the most closely-watched market bulls, is the co-chairman of the Investment policy committee and Goldman Sachs. She said that, although the stock and bond markets expected the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates at its March 25 policy meeting, they still swooned slightly after being jabbed.
"But much of that discomfort is now over as we wait and see how the fundamentals play out," she said.
Cohen said the U.S. economy is still supported by strong fundamentals, with inflation under control and recession nowhere in sight.

She remained comfortable with year-end price targets and had not changed Goldman's asset allocations. Cohen has forecast earnings growth for the Standard & Poor's 500 companies will rise eight to 10 percent in 1997.
Cohen also recommended financial, technology, selected cyclical issues and small- and mid-cap stocks.
The first two sectors were hit very hard over the past two weeks and the final two were well-positioned to perform better in the future.
In the financial sectors, Cohen recommended Citicorp, Chase Manhattan Corp, NationsBank Corp, Banc One Corp, Travelers Group Inc and MBNA Corp.
The recent roughness in the technology sector, as many portfolio managers reached quarter-end and booked profits, was creating an opportunity. She cited Intel Corp, Microsoft Corp and Dell Computer.
Selected cyclical issues could benefit from the growing U.S. domestic economy, including retailers the Gap Inc and Saks Holdings Inc and transport names Delta Air Lines Inc and AMR Corp.

Some small- and mid-cap firms are positioned for growth as portfolio managers become encouraged to "stretch out along that risk curve." She mentioned Stratus Computer Inc, Carmike Cinemas Inc, and Dole Food Co Inc.
